reason: Both verified at source and in the browser. shell.css:101-113 is thirteen absolute px steps; forcing the root to 24px leaves .b-title at 24px and .b-num at 148px, so the reader's one persistent setting is inert. Blast radius is small, not engagement-wide: all 74 font-size declarations go through var(--size-*), that token is used for nothing else, and leading is unitless, so at a 16px root every computed pixel and every audit ramp is unchanged. Separately, build.mjs's template emits no <html> element at all, so documentElement.lang is empty in every state; the fix belongs in build.mjs, not the generated master.
sharpenedFix: Two edits, both at source. (1) build.mjs: emit <html lang="en-IE"> as the template's first line, and assert a non-empty BCP-47 tag in interaction-check.mjs. (2) shell.css: convert only the reading ladder, label through title, eight steps, to rem (11px becomes 0.6875rem, 30px becomes 1.875rem). Leave titleWide, figure, card, count and countWide in px. I drove a full thirteen-step rem ladder at a 24px root: it pushed .b-measureHead, .b-when, .b-field, .b-dayWrap and the device frame into new clipping in day, print and phone, because those counts are composed against a fixed 1180px stage. Re-run audit.mjs and shots.mjs to confirm the 16px render is byte-identical.
